original_question: Does there exist a Hénon map, possibly of some degree, that has a wild attractor: a Cantor invariant set that attracts a subset of positive Lebesgue measure and is strictly contained in a transitive set?
target_in_paper: Section 2.1 (“Strange attractors”), Question 1: the real-dynamical existence problem asking for a Hénon map that admits a wild attractor. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s official formulation: it asks an existence question about a Hénon map, leaves the degree open, and uses the same core description of a wild attractor as a Cantor set attracting a set of positive Lebesgue measure and strictly contained in a transitive set. The added word “invariant” is consistent with the surrounding attractor context. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))
missing_details: The paper places the question in the real setting: Section 2 concerns real Hénon maps, and Berger says more generally entire diffeomorphisms of R^2; the refined question should therefore make the ambient real dynamics explicit. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))

Immediately before Question 1, the paper frames the discussion through measure-theoretical attractors, defined as invariant compact subsets attracting a set of positive Lebesgue measure and minimal with that property; this is the hidden attractor context behind the phrase “wild attractor.” ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))

The official wording is “Can we find a Hénon map (of some degree) ... ?”, so the degree is intentionally unspecified rather than fixed, and Question 1 imposes no dissipativity, Jacobian, or parameter restrictions. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))

To make the question fully stand-alone, it helps to state explicitly that the Cantor set is invariant and that the larger transitive set is for the same real Hénon map. The nearby context supports this, even though the one-line question itself only states the measurable-attraction and strict-inclusion properties. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))
refined_question: Can one find a real Hénon map of some degree on R^2 that admits a wild attractor, namely an invariant Cantor set that attracts a set of positive Lebesgue measure and is strictly contained in a transitive invariant set?
justification: The draft is targeting exactly Question 1 in §2.1, not a broader neighboring problem. The paper’s wording is essentially the same, with the only important implicit addition being that the section is about real Hénon dynamics and that “wild attractor” is being used in the measure-theoretical-attractor sense introduced immediately above. Right after Question 1, the paper notes that Avila and Lyubich have announced a positive answer in the quadratic Hénon family; that remark is contextual and should not replace the official formulation itself. ([math.univ-toulouse.fr](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~buff/Preprints/Henon/Henon.pdf))
